title: deferred-provisioning-contract-and-utilization-surface-calibrator
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience 'fast-provision' oscillations where short-term demand spikes trigger aggressive provisioning followed by immediate scale-downs, which increases cost and leads to jitter for tail latency. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a deferred provisioning contract (DPC) that encodes policy about how long a provisional allocation must survive before it becomes billable/reservable, and 2) a utilization surface calibrator (USC) that models observed utilization as a time‑smoothed surface instead of a single scalar, enabling the autoscaler to make provisioning decisions using shape-aware thresholds (ramp, slope, second derivative) rather than only percentiles. Design: - DPC is a lightweight state machine attached to warm-pool candidates: states {candidate, provisional, committed}. A candidate becomes provisional when predicted aggregated demand crosses a soft threshold; it is promoted to committed only after satisfying a configurable survival window. Promotion includes an idempotent ledger entry used by the reservation accounting service. - USC builds a compact time-series surface per tenant/model by aggregating min/median/max across rolling sub-windows (0–1s, 1–10s, 10–60s). The autoscaler consumes three derived signals: ramp_factor (first diff), curvature (second diff), and persistence_score (survival likelihood). These signals feed a ruleset that biases provisioning: prefer provisional allocations for short high-curvature spikes, commit when persistence_score > policy.threshold. Implementation highlights: - pkg/autoscaler/dpc.go: state machine, contract API, and ledger integration hooks. - pkg/autoscaler/util_surface.go: surface construction, smoothing kernels, sampling backfill for sparse tenants. - controllers/warmpool_controller.go: orchestration changes to prefer provisional -> staged promotion path. - telemetry/exporters/util_surface_prometheus.go: exposes ramp_factor/curvature/persistence_score per-tenant and aggregated 1h/24h histograms. - cmd/fleetctl/inspect-dpc: diagnostic CLI to inspect provisional commitments, useful for on-call and capacity planning. Backwards compatibility: DPC defaults to a conservative 30s survival window and disabled ledger promotion for accounts without committed reservations to avoid billing semantics changes. Feature is guarded behind config flag autoscaler.deferred_provisioning.enabled (off in existing clusters by default). Testing and validation: - Unit tests cover state transitions (candidate -> provisional -> committed), race windows for concurrent predictions, and failure recovery when promotion RPC fails and is retried. - Integration tests (kind/e2e) simulate synthetic workloads with deterministic spikes: low-frequency long spikes vs microbursts. - Perf microbenchmarks: measurement harness shows median decision latency increase of 120µs and a 6% reduction in cold-boot provisioning events under mixed workloads. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind rollout flag. - Start canary on a small dedicated cluster and enable telemetry dashboards for ramp_factor/curvature. - Monitor commit rate vs provisional rate, p95 latency, and cost per token. - After 2 weeks of stable signals enable for 25% of fleets, then 100% with conservative defaults. Migration notes: No schema changes to reservation ledger. Operators wanting older behavior can set autoscaler.deferred_provisioning.enabled=false. Related work: complements tenant-weighting and headroom controllers; see ENG-1729 for historical demand forecasting improvements.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) add a unit test that simulates a flaky promotion RPC and ensures we don't double-commit; (2) can we avoid sampling at 100Hz for small tenants to limit memory?
Maya Patel: Added retry-idempotency and switched to adaptive sampling that drops to 10Hz for <10 concurrent shards. PTAL.
Sofia Martinez: Telemetry shape looks good but we need alerting guidance in the docs for 'provisional commit ratio' going >50%.
Maya Patel: Added docs section 'Observability and Alerts' with provisional/commit ratio dashboards and thresholds. Also added RBAC check to fleetctl to avoid leaking ledger info.
Arun Gupta: Approve after nits - prefer naming 'persistence_score' -> 'survival_score' for consistency with forecasting module.
Maya Patel: Renamed metric to survival_score across exports and tests.
CI Bot: integration tests flaky on linux-arm; re-ran and all checks passed.
ci_checks: perf: pass (bench show 6% reduction in cold boots for mixed workloads)
release_notes: Introduce Deferred Provisioning Contract (feature-flagged) and Utilization Surface Calibrator. Default: disabled. Improves provisioning stability and reduces cold-boot events for mixed workloads. Observability: new metrics ramp_factor, curvature, survival_score.
notes_for_oncall: If provisional -> committed promotion spikes unexpectedly: check autoscaler.deferred_provisioning.enabled, inspect cmd/fleetctl inspect-dpc output, verify ledger RPC latencies, and look at survival_score time series for rapid curvature changes.
diagnostics_cli_examples:
# list provisional commitments
fleetctl inspect-dpc --tenant tenant-123 --since 1h
# show util-surface summary
fleetctl util-surface summarize --tenant tenant-123 --window 10m
